text:
Amelia: Heads-up — launching a new Dedicated pool type today: L4p (low-cost inference optimized for small-to-medium seq lengths). Rolling out region-by-region; first wave: us-central1-b and eu-west3-c. :tada:
Amelia: Key things: 1) L4p pools are cheaper per-token for short sequences, 2) support prefix/KV caching and dynamic batching, 3) available for Reserved and burstable ephemeral reservations.
Amelia: Because this is a new SKU, we’re also introducing "burst credits" — short-term extra capacity customers can draw against for spikes without extending reserved commits. Burst credits are free during beta.
Amelia: Policy updates (effective immediately): 
- Default per-org reserved L4p capacity: 8 GPUs.
- Default burst credits allocation: 2 GPU-equivalents.
- To request higher limits please fill the quota request form or ping CS with use-case and expected QPS.
Amelia: GA timeline: beta opens today (whitelisted). General availability targeted in ~6 weeks, depending on early beta feedback.
Amelia: Quick CLI example to reserve in beta: 
```
redwoodctl dedicated reserve --pool l4p --zone us-central1-b --count 2 --duration 30d --billing-account ACCT-123
```
Amelia: Console path: https://console.redwood.ai/dedicated/pools/l4p (internal doc + FAQ linked in the thread).

deploy-bot: Reservation service ready checks passed in us-central1-b and eu-west3-c. health: OK

Jonathan: Congrats team! Quick q: how does L4p pricing compare to existing L4 and A10g tiers?

Amelia: Jonathan: estimated guidance for beta (per-GPU/hr, billed per-second): L4p ~ $0.06–0.09/hr, L4 ~ $0.12–0.18/hr, A10g ~ $0.35–0.50/hr. Final GA pricing may change, will publish on pricing page. Also note burst usage is metered separately.

Mica: SRE note — expected SLOs for L4p (beta): P95 latency target for typical text-gen requests 120–160ms for short prefixes; P99 under light load may spike to ~400ms until auto-batch stabilizes. We’ll run canaries and notify if any regressions. Planned maintenance window for rollout day: 02:00–04:00 UTC tonight for the eu-west3-c boot strapping.

Kevin: Sales — do we have a short customer-facing blurb and FAQ we can use in outreach? Any contraindications for regulated workloads on L4p?

Emily-CS: Kevin: CS has a draft one-pager and email template. Short answer re: regulated workloads — L4p supports Dedicated reservations (data isolated), but Private (VPC) option not yet enabled for L4p in this beta. If customers need VPC/on-prem, advise Dedicated H200/A100 families instead. Email for quota or enterprise requests: redwood-cs@redwood.ai.

Ops-oncall: Adding monitoring playbook to the incident runbook: new dashboards (P95/P99, batch size, cache hit rate) and an alert if P95 increases >50% over baseline for >5min. I’ll watch first 24h and escalate.

Amelia: Action items: 
- Eng: monitor canaries and share telemetry in eng-runtime channel.
- CS & Sales: use the one-pager + template from Emily for beta invites.
- Docs: publishing FAQ + example workloads in 2h.
- Support: accept quota requests and add to the whitelist.

Amelia: Note on legacy pools: we will mark old "L4-legacy" pools as deprecated in 90 days; customers on L4-legacy should plan migrations — we’ll provide a migration guide and a compatibility flag in the runtime to smooth transition.

Amelia: Questions or issues, ping me or @ops-oncall. Internal FAQ: https://docs.internal.redwood.ai/dedicated/l4p-beta (internal). :information_source:
